items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: when I started out playing guitar there were no women I could look at except Sister Rosetta Tharpe... these people, these women play guitar. And that meant a lot to me

ctx.x: Did Mary Lou Williams also — I don’t want to read anything into that — but did she represent something to you being a woman professional musician?

You know it’s absolutely true, I’m not sure I made the connection. But I know particularly — because I didn’t start out playing piano. And when I started out playing guitar there were no women I could look at except Sister Rosetta Tharpe and of course Memphis Minnie were the only two who I could look to and say these people, these women play guitar. And when I was just learning to play guitar I was I think a junior in high school. And I had this wonderful boyfriend who turned me on to just all kinds of wonderful…

Was there a — this may sound silly, but — was there an issue as far as being a non- feminine thing to do? Like if you play guitar you can’t grow your nails long, right? And in junior high — you were like not concerned about it?
